Look up each plugin there; the entry will tell you if it works out-of-the-box, if there’s a fork/MapLibre-specific version, or if you need to replace it with an alternative. Below is a step-by-step guide for checking your plugins, what to do when a plugin doesn’t work, and a quick reference of the most common Mapbox plugins and their current MapLibre status (as of MapLibre v6). --- ## 1️⃣ Start with the official compatibility list | 👉 **What to do** | 👉 **Why it matters** | |-------------------|----------------------| | Open the **awesome-maplibre** repository: | It is the curated, up-to-date catalogue of plugins, UI components, and utilities that have been tested with MapLibre. | | Use the repository’s search (⌘ F / Ctrl F) for the name of each Mapbox plugin you use. | Each entry tells you one of three things:
• **Works unchanged** – you can keep the same import and code.
• **Forked / MapLibre-specific version** – install the forked package (often the same name with a `-maplibre` suffix).
• **No MapLibre support** – you’ll need an alternative. | | If a plugin is **not listed**, treat it as “unknown”. Test it (see step 3) and, if it fails, either open an issue on the plugin repo or look for a MapLibre-compatible replacement. | The list is community-driven; missing entries are common for very new or very niche plugins. | --- ## 2️⃣ Typical categories & what to look for | Category | Typical Mapbox plugin name | What to check on awesome-maplibre | |----------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------| | **Controls / UI widgets** | `mapbox-gl-geocoder`, `mapbox-gl-draw`, `mapbox-gl-compare`, `mapbox-gl-rtl-text` | Usually have a fork (`@maplibre/mapbox-gl-geocoder`, `@maplibre/mapbox-gl-draw`) or work unchanged. | | **Heatmaps / clustering** | `mapbox-gl-heatmap`, `supercluster` (used via Mapbox source) | Heatmap layer type is native; clustering works with any GeoJSON source. | | **3-D / terrain** | `mapbox-gl-terrain`, `mapbox-gl-extrude` | `mapbox-gl-terrain` works unchanged (it just adds a raster-DEM source). | | **Animation / time-slider** | `mapbox-gl-animate`, `mapbox-gl-timeline` | Look for a fork or a generic WebGL animation library; many are UI-only and work as-is. | | **Search / geocoder UI** | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` | Forked as `@maplibre/mapbox-gl-geocoder` (same API). | | **Data-driven styling helpers** | `mapbox-gl-style-switcher`, `mapbox-gl-legend` | Often UI-only; they usually work unchanged after you replace the namespace. | | **Custom source adapters** | `mapbox-gl-source-xyz`, `mapbox-gl-source-wmts` | Verify that the source type (`vector`, `raster`, `geojson`) is still supported; the adapter code may reference `mapboxgl` globals – replace with `maplibregl`. | If the entry on awesome-maplibre says **“Works with MapLibre vX+”**, you can keep the same import (just change the namespace). If it says **“MapLibre fork available”**, install the forked package and follow its README (often the API is identical). If it says **“No support / use alternative”**, you’ll need to replace it (see the “Alternatives” section below). --- ## 3️⃣ Quick sanity-check after you swap the core library Even when a plugin is listed as compatible, a few practical steps help you avoid runtime errors: 1. **Update the import style** – MapLibre v6 ships **ES-modules only**.    import MapboxGeocoder from '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder';
   ```js
   // MapLibre (if the same package works)
   import MapboxGeocoder from '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder';
   // or, if a fork exists:
   import MapLibreGeocoder from '@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder';
   ```

2. **Replace the namespace** – change every `mapboxgl` reference in the plugin’s usage to `maplibregl`.  
   ```js
   // before
   const geocoder = new MapboxGeocoder({ accessToken: mapboxgl.accessToken });
   // after
   const geocoder = new MapLibreGeocoder({ /* no accessToken needed */ });
   ```

3. **Remove the token** – most UI plugins no longer need a token; if the plugin’s constructor still asks for one, just omit it or pass an empty string.

4. **Run the app** – open the page, watch the console for errors like `mapboxgl is not defined` or `Unsupported source type: mapbox://`. Those indicate a Mapbox-only dependency that must be replaced.

5. **Check CSS** – UI plugins often ship their own CSS that uses the `mapboxgl-` prefix. If you see missing styles, replace the prefix in the CSS (or import the plugin’s MapLibre-specific stylesheet if it ships one).

---

## 3️⃣ Common plugins & MapLibre equivalents

Below is a “cheat-sheet” of the most frequently-used Mapbox plugins and what you’ll typically do when migrating. If your plugin isn’t listed, follow the steps in section 2.

| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw** | ✅ works after namespace change | Install the same package; just replace `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl`. |
| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder** | 🔀 fork exists | Use `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` (same API). |
| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-compare** | ✅ works (no token) | Just change imports; CSS class prefix change (`mapboxgl-compare` → `maplibregl-compare`). |
| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-rtl-text** | ✅ works (auto-loaded) | No change needed; MapLibre already bundles RTL support. |
| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-js** (the core) | N/A – you’re replacing it | Use `maplibre-gl`. |
| **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-js/plugins/MapboxDirections** | ❌ incompatible (uses Mapbox Directions API) | Switch to **OpenRouteService**, **OSRM**, or **MapTiler Directions**. UI control can be built with the same `maplibregl.Control` pattern. |

> *❌* – the plugin depends on Mapbox-only services (tiles, APIs, token). You’ll need to replace it with a different library or roll your own.

Since **MapLibre GL JS v6** ships **ES-modules only**, many older plugins that still import the UMD bundle (`import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'`) will break. Do the following:

1. **Add a peer dependency** on `maplibre-gl` in the plugin’s `package.json` (if you fork it).  
2. **Use named imports** if the plugin supports them:  
   ```js
   import { Map } from 'maplibre-gl';
   ```
3. **If the plugin ships its own bundled UMD file**, replace the script tag with the ES-module version (or use a bundler like Vite/Rollup/Webpack to resolve the ES-module entry point).

| Option | When to use it | What you need to do |
|--------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Self-host / fork the plugin** | The plugin is small, well-documented, and you can modify the source. | Clone the repo, replace all `mapboxgl` references, remove token usage, publish to your own npm scope (or use `npm link`). |

4. **If ❌** – look for an alternative in the same section of awesome-maplibre, or plan a fork/self-host.

```bash
# 2️⃣ Install the MapLibre fork

```


```js
import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';

  style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty',
  center: [-122.42, 37.78],
  zoom: 12
});

  placeholder: 'Search places…',

});

```

* import path,  
* namespace (`maplibregl`),  
* removal of the token,  
* optional `maplibregl` reference passed to the control (required by the fork).

---

## 8️⃣ Final sanity-check

After you have updated **all** plugins:

```bash
npm run build   # or your bundler’s dev command
npm start       # open the app
```

* Verify that every control appears and works (drag, click, search, draw, etc.).  
* Open the browser console and confirm there are **no** `ReferenceError: mapboxgl is not defined` or `Unsupported source type: mapbox://` messages.  
* If you see a missing sprite/glyph error, double-check that your style URL (see the migration guide) points to a style that provides its own sprite and glyph URLs – MapLibre will not fetch Mapbox-hosted assets.

---

### TL;DR

1. **Check awesome-maplibre** for each plugin → ✅, 🔀, or ❌.  
2. **Rename imports & namespaces** (`mapboxgl` → `maplibregl`).  
3. **Remove the Mapbox access token**; configure any service-specific keys separately.  
4. **Swap to a MapLibre-compatible style** (non-`mapbox://`).  
5. **If a plugin is ❌**, either use the listed fork/alternative or rewrite/fork it yourself.  

Following those steps will let you keep the same UI/UX you built with Mapbox while moving to the fully open-source, token-free MapLibre ecosystem. Happy mapping!
